correctness.rationale: PASS: Comparing the Rota-Baxter identity on (v,v), (1,1), and (1,v) forces the scalar parts to vanish and \(T^2=0\); in characteristic two the remaining \(2T(u)\) condition is vacuous. Sufficiency follows by direct substitution. Rank-r square-zero maps correspond bijectively to flags U⊆K with dimensions r,n-r and a vector-space isomorphism V/K→U. Explicit centralizer blocks are transitive on four and only four vector strata; their cardinalities sum to \(q^n\). \(P^2(a+v)\)=aT(u), \(P^3=0\) and index-three examples require n≥2. Exhaustive independent RB-equation and GL-conjugacy checks pass for (q,n)=(2,1),(3,1),(2,2),(3,2),(2,3); the odd controls are not treated as characteristic-two proofs.

originality.rationale: PASS within accessible literature: Gubarev 2018 studies broad nilpotence but not these finite-field square-zero-local orbit counts. Farooq 2026 Theorem 3.4 concerns the identical local algebra only in characteristic zero and explicitly requires \(T(u)=0\); it does not imply the characteristic-two extra strata or the orbit-size distribution. Zheng–Guo–Rosenkranz 2019 treat characteristic-zero semigroup-algebra cases of fixed small order. A published finite-exterior-algebra characteristic-two classification has nonzero radical products and hence distinct Rota–Baxter constraints. Targeted published-finding corpus, arXiv and full-text searches found no dominating all-even-field classification. Residual risk: unindexed equivalences; a public summary of the exterior case was accessible, not its complete source.

value.rationale: PASS: The theorem determines the natural finite-field automorphism-orbit-size distribution of Rota–Baxter operators on every first-order thickening of a rational point, uniformly in both embedding dimension and even field size. More importantly, it isolates and exactly enumerates the genuinely characteristic-two obstruction to the square-zero-operator description known in characteristic zero, including a sharp index-three jump. The all-dimensional classification and orbit sizes are structurally informative rather than a renaming of a low-dimensional census.
